awd_titl_txt: REU Site: Gluing Computer Science and Convex Geometry: Research Experiences for Undergraduates from Community Colleges
awd_abstract_narration:
This REU Site aims at providing undergraduate Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) students with a unique combination of research and hands-on laboratory and deployment experiences in the area of wireless sensor networks at Texas A&M University-Kingsville. Specifically, this new Site focuses on strengthening the synergy between computer science and convex geometry through a truly multidisciplinary environment. This REU Site includes a set of well-defined and challenging research projects, which are tight to a wide variety of real-world applications, with an emphasis on the problems of connected k-coverage, data collection, and geographic forwarding in both two-dimensional and three-dimensional wireless sensor networks. The major goal of this REU Site is to help the recruited undergraduate students get exposure to several valuable research tools and experiences in the above-mentioned research areas so as to become science and engineering statespersons for their generation.

This new REU Site will help recruit undergraduate students from various U.S. institutions having limited research opportunities with a more focus on underrepresented ones, including Black, Hispanic, female, disable, low-income, and first-generation students, who traditionally have been underrepresented in science and engineering. These are talented undergraduate students who are interested in research as well as hands-on laboratory and deployment experiences in the areas of computer science, convex geometry, and wireless sensor networks for this REU Site. This summer research experience for these students early in their academic career will certainly benefit them significantly. Indeed, research for undergraduates can be viewed as a high-impact educational practice that is capable of producing positive outcomes for these students, such as student independence and self-confidence, career interest reinforcement, integration into their selected field; conducting experiments; analyzing data; communicating results; and working with others as a team. In addition, this type of research experience provides interactions between faculty and students, which in turn facilitate personal connections between them; improves student retention and learning experience; and enhances the quality of the undergraduate curriculum. The findings of this REU Site can be disseminated using local, national, and international conferences, and also published in highly reputed journals.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Our NSF REU Site produced 17 publications:

  • 15 Conference papers
  • 2 Journal papers

We received two prestigious awards at the IEEE PICom 2025, Hakodate, Hokkaido, Japan, October 21-24, 2025:

  • IEEE Best Paper Award
  • IEEE Best Student Paper Award

Summer 2025 Publications

1. Cecilia Duran* and Habib M. Ammari, "A Hybrid Nature-Inspired Algorithm for Establishing Reliable Connected Coverage,” 29th Conference on Innovation in Clouds, Internet and Networks “Disruptive Intelligent Technologies for Next-Generation Clouds and Networks”,  Athens, Greece, March 30 – April 02, 2026.

2. David Jason Cruz Santiago* and Habib M. Ammari, “An Efficient and Cost-Aware Approach to Hole Restoration in Heterogeneous Wireless Sensor Networks Using Geometric Inversion,” 17th  IEEE Latin American Symposium on Circuits and Systems (IEEE LASCAS), Arequipa, Peru, February 24 – 27, 2026.

3. Joseph R. Rodriguez* and Habib M. Ammari, "Precision Hole Detection and Energy-Aware QoS Scheduling for Wireless Sensor Networks,” The 14th  IFIP/IEEE International Conference on Performance Evaluation and Modeling in Wired and Wireless Networks (IFIP/IEEE PEMWN), Paris, France, November 25-27, 2025.

4. David Jason Cruz Santiago* and Habib M. Ammari, “An Efficient Geometric Inversion Based Approach to Hole Detection and Restoration in Wireless Sensor Networks,” 16th IFIP Wireless and Mobile Networking Conference (WMNC), Leuven, Belgium, November 27-28, 2025.

5. Roberto D. Esquivel* and Habib M. Ammari, "Q-Learning-Based Sensor Selection for k-Coverage in Wireless Sensor Networks,” The 10th National Workshop for REU Research in Networking and Systems (REUNS 2025), Co-located with the 22nd IEEE International Conference on Mobile Ad-Hoc and Smart Systems Conference (IEEE MASS), Chicago, USA, October 6, 2025.

6. Jorge R. Rodriguez* and Habib M. Ammari, "k-Coverage in Three-Dimensional Wireless Sensor Networks Using a Game Theoretical Approach,” The 10th National Workshop for REU Research in Networking and Systems (REUNS 2025), Co-located with the 22nd IEEE International Conference on Mobile Ad-Hoc and Smart Systems Conference (IEEE MASS), Chicago, USA, October 6, 2025.

7. David W. Starr* and Habib M. Ammari, “ORCHID: Tessellation-based cylindrical deployment protocol for energy-efficient coverage in three-dimensional wireless sensor networks,” The 21st International Conference on Wireless and Mobile Computing, Networking and Communications (WiMob), Marrakesh, Morocco, October 20-22, 2025.

Summer 2024 Publications

8. Scott A. Whitman* and Habib M. Ammari, “Using optimized tiling schemes for attaining k-coverage in wireless sensor networks,” The 23rd IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Intelligence and Computing (IEEE PICom), Hakodate City, Hokkaido, Japan, October 21-24, 2025.

9. Kellen O'Rourke* and Habib M. Ammari, “MAGIk: Minimizing Active Sensors Using Modified Genetic Algorithm with Improved Mutation for k-Coverage and Connectivity,” The 15th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Ubiquitous Networking (ICMU), Busan, Korea, September 10-12, 2025.

10. Edward Strong* and Habib M. Ammari, “A homological criterion for k-coverage in wireless sensor networks with controlled boundaries,” Seventh  International Conference of the Tunisian Operational Research Society (TORS), Sousse, Tunisia, April 11-13, 2025.

11. Edward Strong* and Habib M. Ammari, “A homological criterion for k-coverage in wireless sensor networks with controlled boundaries,” Lecture Notes in Operations Research - Advances in Operations Research Theory, Algorithms, and Applications, Springer (Selected from the Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference of the Tunisian Operational Research Society (IC_TORS’25), Tunisia, April 11–13, 2025).

12. Jonathan B. Davenport, Joshua Chikosha*, and Habib M. Ammari, “Optimizing target coverage in wireless sensor networks: A hybrid differential evolution and simulated annealing-based approach,” Springer LNCS Proceedings of International Conference on Internet of Things (ICIOT), Bangkok, Thailand, November 16 - 19, 2024.

Summer 2023 Publications

13. Tianjian Li, Bill Huynh*, and Habib M. Ammari, “Toward Establishing Sensing k-Coverage: A Points Placement with Separation and Minimum Enclosing Circle-Based Approach,” The 23rd IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Intelligence and Computing (IEEE PICom), Hakodate City, Hokkaido, Japan, October 21-24, 2025 (IEEE Best Paper Award!).

14. Gavin L. Moore, Kellen O'Rourke*, and Habib M. Ammari, “SMAMCS: Simulated Multi-Agents for Mobile k-Coverage in Sparse Wireless Sensor Networks,” The 23rd IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Intelligence and Computing (IEEE PICom), Hakodate City, Hokkaido, Japan, October 21-24, 2025 (IEEE Best Student Paper Award!).

15. Alwin M. Kurian, Munachimso Onuorah*, and Habib M. Ammari, "Optimizing coverage in wireless sensor networks: A binary ant colony algorithm with hill climbing,” Special Issue "Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANET) in the Era of Cutting Edge Technologies", Applied Sciences, 14(3), 960, January 2024.

16. Syed Zaidi, Kevin Gutama*, and Habib M. Ammari, "GAMA: Genetic algorithm for k-coverage and connectivity with minimum sensor activation in wireless sensor networks,” 16th Annual International Conference on Combinatorial Optimization and Applications (COCOA), Honolulu, Hawaii, USA, December 15-17, 2023.
